summary:
The Prophet

Kahlil Gibran's influential 1923 book, 'The Prophet', is a seminal work of prose poetry that has had a lasting impact on modern literature and culture. This Lebanese-American poet and writer drew upon his experiences living in the United States and his exploration of Eastern mysticism to create a collection of 26 short fables that have been translated into over 40 languages.

Through its vivid imagery, metaphors, and exploration of universal themes such as love, freedom, and the human condition, 'The Prophet' has resonated with readers across cultures and time zones. Gibran's innovative style and his emphasis on the importance of individualism, spirituality, and self-discovery have made him one of the most beloved and respected writers of the 20th century.

Gibran's work has also been influential in shaping modern art, music, and film, with its themes and imagery continuing to inspire artists and audiences today.





The Prophet was first published in 1923 by Alfred A. Knopf and went on to become a bestseller, selling over 20 million copies worldwide. It has been translated into many languages and remains one of the most widely read and influential books of the 20th century.
